newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Euro-presidency rejects 'Europe a la carte'.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Euro-presidency rejects 'Europe a la carte'.

text.p: Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok on Saturday rejected the idea of a "Europe a la carte", saying European member states should decide the future of the Union together.
"A Europe a la carte...is not what the Dutch presidency wants," Kok told a news conference after informal talks with British opposition Labour Party leader Tony Blair.

Kok said talks with Blair, in The Netherlands to address a conference on European social policy, had dealt with the issue of flexibility, the degree to which individual European member states embrace new legislation.
Europe's 15 member states were still hammering out what flexibility should entail, Kok said.
But he added that Europe a la carte where just a few countries could decide how they wished to proceed was unacceptable.
Blair said he would not support flexibility if it entailed a permanent multi-tier Europe.
If flexibility meant a group of countries going ahead, with Britain or other countries permanently "excluded from the high table", Labour would reject it, he said.

Kok, who heads the Dutch Labour PvdA party, would not be drawn on whether a British Labour government would make a better European negotiating partner than the ruling Conservative administration, known to be battling with internal rifts over Europe.
"We are dealing with only one negotiating partner and that is the British government...it is up to the British people to decide who their next government will be," Kok said.
